grades.quote: The most important characterization of a given memory address range is whether it holds regular main memory or I/O devices. Regular main memory is required to have a number of properties, specified below, whereas I/O devices can have a much broader range of attributes.
grades.reason: Explains the main-memory versus I/O classification, but not how cacheability relates to it.

grades.quote: The cacheability of a memory region should not affect the software view of the region except for differences reflected in other PMAs, such as main memory versus I/O classification, memory ordering, supported accesses and atomic operations, and coherence.
grades.reason: Directly distinguishes cacheability from main-memory/I/O classification and identifies the architectural attributes governing observable access behavior.
